title: Meta Hits Record Sales, but Stock Slides on AI Costs
summary: Meta reported record second-quarter sales of $60.8 billion, but its stock fell after the company said it would raise the minimum spending on its AI infrastructure buildout by $5 billion for the year. Investors remain focused on whether the pace of AI capital spending is sustainable.

title: Microsoft Beats Wall Street Expectations, With 31% Jump in Profits
summary: Microsoft closed its fiscal year with about $90 billion in quarterly sales and a 31% jump in profit, beating Wall Street expectations. Investors remain focused on whether the company's record data-center buildout will ultimately pay off.

title: A Backlash Against Anthropic Is Brewing in Silicon Valley
summary: Startup founders and researchers are growing wary of Anthropic, criticizing the AI company for launching products that compete directly with firms in its own ecosystem and for warnings about open-weight models that critics say aim to hobble rivals rather than address safety. Some critics allege the company is using safety concerns to seek favorable regulation.

title: Visa Is Cutting 2,600 Jobs, About 7% of Its Workforce
summary: Visa is cutting roughly 2,600 jobs, about 7% of its workforce, as CEO Ryan McInerney told employees in a memo that changing payments technology has created a "once-in-a-lifetime inflection point" requiring the company to evolve how it operates.

title: OpenAI, Anthropic Endorse Letter Asking US to Help Pace AI Development
summary: More than 1,100 senior executives and employees at leading AI firms, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki, signed a letter urging the U.S. government to support an international mechanism to deliberately pace frontier AI development. The signatories warned that automating AI research could accelerate capability gains beyond humans' ability to understand or control the resulting systems, days after an OpenAI model breached the Hugging Face repository during a security test.

title: With AI, Hackers Revive Attacks on VPNs
summary: AI tools are supercharging a hacking strategy first used during the pandemic, making attacks on corporate virtual private networks cheaper, faster and more effective. Prolonged work-from-home habits continue to leave VPNs a persistent target for intrusion into corporate networks.

title: Coordinated Cyberattack Hits at Least 30 Minnesota Water Facilities
summary: U.S. and Minnesota authorities are investigating a coordinated cyberattack on at least 30 water-treatment facilities that began earlier in the week. Some operations were disrupted, but officials said there was no need for residents to change their water use, and state and federal responders are coordinating to contain the incident.

title: Trump Administration Bans New Humanoid Robots From China
summary: The U.S. government banned imports of new foreign-made humanoid robots, most of which come from China, citing national security risks. The FCC added humanoid and quadruped robots to its list of equipment posing security threats, blocking new models from receiving import authorization, though previously authorized robots already in use are unaffected.

title: PayPal CEO Says 'Open' to Evaluating Deal Offers
summary: PayPal CEO Enrique Lores said the company remains open to evaluating acquisition offers while pursuing its turnaround strategy, following an unsolicited buyout offer from Stripe and Advent International earlier this month of more than $53 billion, or $60.50 per share. PayPal reported second-quarter net revenue of $8.7 billion, up 5% year over year, while net income fell 12% to $1.1 billion; shares rose 4.3%.

title: Meta and BlackRock Partner on $14bn El Paso Data Center
summary: Meta is bringing in BlackRock to finance much of its El Paso, Texas data center campus, with BlackRock-managed funds acquiring an 80% ownership stake partly financed through $12.5 billion in debt while Meta retains a 20% stake. The deal reflects how large tech companies increasingly rely on external financing alongside their own capital to fund rapid AI infrastructure expansion; the campus is expected to become operational in 2028.

title: TSMC's Japan Plant Gradually Resumes Operation After Earthquake
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. said it is gradually resuming operations at its Kumamoto, Japan plant after a magnitude-7 earthquake struck the region. Building structures were reported safe, though detailed inspections continue; construction on a nearby second plant was largely unaffected, with some work paused as a precaution against aftershocks.

title: Amazon Hires Google TPU Veteran to Work on Trainium Software
summary: Amazon hired Robert Hundt, the original software lead for Google's Tensor Processing Unit chips, to work on its Neuron software for Trainium AI chips. It is the second senior Google hardware hire for Amazon's chip team in three months as Amazon competes with Nvidia's CUDA ecosystem.

title: Commvault Shares Drop on Growth Slowdown
summary: Commvault shares fell 16% after the data backup and recovery software firm reported revenue growth slowed to 11% year-over-year ($314 million) in its July quarter, down from 13% growth the prior quarter. The company maintained its forecast for about 19% annualized recurring revenue growth in fiscal 2027.

title: Nvidia Bet on Reflection for Open-Source AI. Now the Startup Is Playing Catch-Up.
summary: Nvidia-backed startup Reflection AI is racing to catch up with U.S. and Chinese rivals as it seeks to become America's leading open-source AI champion, according to The Information.

title: OpenAI's ChatGPT Nears 1 Billion Weekly Active Users Seven Months After Target
summary: OpenAI's ChatGPT is approaching 1 billion weekly active users, seven months later than the company's original internal target. It remains among the fastest internet applications ever to reach that scale, doing so less than four years after launch.

title: SpaceXAI Explores Major Data Center Expansion in Texas
summary: SpaceXAI is exploring a major expansion of its data center footprint in Texas as part of the broader race among AI companies to secure computing infrastructure, according to The Information.

title: Oracle Data Centers Face Multibillion-Dollar Cost Surprises
summary: Oracle is confronting multibillion-dollar cost overruns on a proposed $165 billion AI data center supercampus, The Information reports, underscoring the ballooning capital costs large tech companies face as they race to build AI infrastructure.

title: Cenovus CEO Says New Trilateral Agreement Makes Oilsands Growth Investable Again
summary: Cenovus Energy CEO Jon McKenzie said a new non-binding trilateral memorandum between the Oil Sands Alliance and the federal and Alberta governments makes oilsands growth "investable again," a marked shift from his comments last month calling a proposed West Coast pipeline "unfinanceable." The remarks came as Cenovus reported second-quarter profit of $2.87 billion, up sharply from $851 million a year earlier, driven by stronger oil prices.

title: Brookfield and NextEra to Build a US$100B Data-Centre Campus in Kentucky
summary: Brookfield and NextEra Energy are building a data center and power campus on the site of a former Cold War uranium-enrichment plant in western Kentucky, including a two-gigawatt natural gas plant, up to 2.6 gigawatts of battery storage, and 1.8 gigawatts of AI computing capacity. The project is part of Brookfield's broader roughly $100 billion push into AI infrastructure, for which it is also raising a dedicated $10 billion fund backed in part by Nvidia.

title: Energy Companies Suffer the Most Expensive Cyber Breaches, IBM Finds
summary: The average cost of a successful cyberattack on a Canadian firm reached $7.11 million this year, up from $6.98 million last year, according to an IBM survey of organizations breached between March 2025 and February 2026. Energy companies fared worst, with average breach costs of $9.21 million, as attacks increasingly target critical infrastructure and supply chains.

title: AT&T Completes $23B EchoStar Spectrum Buy
summary: AT&T completed a $23 billion acquisition of spectrum assets from EchoStar, which the company said will boost 5G capacity across the U.S. and enhance its ability to meet emerging AI-driven network demand.

title: AT&T Bets on Routing, Open Model to Tame AI Costs
summary: AT&T detailed how it is managing the cost and performance trade-offs of running AI at scale, outlining a proprietary AI gateway designed to cut costs by up to 90% through smarter routing and use of open models.

title: Amazon Data Centres Damaged in Bahrain
summary: Two Amazon data centers in Bahrain were damaged in an attack that Bloomberg reported was allegedly carried out by Iran in response to the company's support for U.S. military operations.

title: Bain, Tillman Invest $1.5B in Eaton Fiber for Verizon Expansion
summary: Bain Capital and Tillman Global Holdings announced a $1.5 billion investment in Eaton Fiber, Verizon's exclusive wholesale fiber-building partner, to fund Eaton's acquisition of Ripple Fiber and the next phase of its network expansion. The deal supports Verizon's asset-light strategy of expanding its fiber footprint to more than 1 million additional locations without directly funding construction.

title: Amazon Asks FCC Approval for 5,000-Satellite Mobile Network
summary: Amazon asked the FCC to approve a direct-to-device network of up to 5,105 low-Earth-orbit satellites to provide global mobile connectivity, with deployment expected to begin in 2028. The move follows Amazon's planned $11.6 billion acquisition of satellite operator Globalstar and puts it in more direct competition with SpaceX's Starlink.

title: OpenAI: How AI Is Expanding Work
summary: OpenAI published a report drawing on 800,000 U.S. work-related ChatGPT messages, finding that 16.8% of all work-related messages and 43.5% of occupation-specific ones involve tasks historically tied to a different occupation, a pattern the company calls "task crossover." The effect is strongest at smaller firms, suggesting workers are testing new task combinations with AI before employers formally redefine roles.

title: IBM: Redesign for Enterprise AI
summary: IBM and Oxford Economics surveyed 1,000 technology executives and AI transformation leaders, finding only 37% of AI initiatives had delivered the business outcomes senior leadership originally expected by the end of 2025, with 21% of AI ROI lost to friction between IT and business units. Just 17% of executives said AI approval and funding processes were consistent across their organization.

title: Meta's Case for Its AI Spending Keeps Getting Weaker
summary: Meta shares fell while Microsoft's rallied after the two companies sent very different signals on how they are monetizing massive AI investments during second-quarter earnings. Meta's all-out AI spending splurge is running into higher costs, borrowing constraints and investor pushback, even as the company points to plans to grow its enterprise AI business.

title: Apple Sales Exceed $109 Billion, Driven by Strong iPhone Sales Growth
summary: Apple reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of about $109 billion, a new quarterly record driven by strong iPhone sales, while continuing to contend with higher component costs. The company is also set to release an upgraded Siri assistant this fall.

title: Amazon Shares Jump as Cloud Sales Accelerate
summary: Amazon Web Services revenue grew 37% year-over-year in the second quarter, its fastest growth rate in roughly 18 quarters, as AI-driven demand lifted cloud computing sales. Amazon shares rose sharply after the results were released.

title: The Rise of Million-Dollar Companies With Just One Employee
summary: AI tools are making it easier for founders to launch and scale companies without hiring staff, with some solo-run businesses reaching seven-figure revenue. One example cited is a company launched last December that has added 10,000 paying customers and is on track for $10 million in revenue this year without any additional employees, using AI to handle customer emails, coding, support requests and subscriptions.

title: IBM Claims New Era of 'Quantum Advantage'
summary: IBM announced joint demonstrations with partners, including Algorithmiq and the University of Chicago, showing quantum computers solving problems considered impractical for classical supercomputers. One demonstration reportedly encoded 70 logical qubits and completed a calculation in about 15 minutes that would take infeasibly long on classical machines.

title: Amazon Ties North Korea to Hacks of Open-Source Software
summary: Amazon researchers linked a North Korea-affiliated hacking group to four separate compromises of open-source JavaScript packages dating back to March 2025, including the widely used axios library, which receives more than 100 million downloads per week. The attackers reportedly gained access by socially engineering trusted package maintainers before publishing malicious updates that were pulled automatically into downstream software.

title: Exclusive: Neocloud Nscale Gets Ready to Pitch Investors on Multibillion-Dollar IPO
summary: Nscale, a UK-based cloud infrastructure provider whose customers reportedly include OpenAI and Microsoft, is moving ahead with plans for a multibillion-dollar IPO despite a jittery stock market that is otherwise unfriendly to new public listings. The company has separately been in talks to acquire a large U.S. data center site to support its AI infrastructure buildout.

title: New Microsoft Copilot Security Flaws Show How AI Can Leak Customer Secrets
summary: Security researchers identified new vulnerabilities in Microsoft Copilot that could allow AI agents to leak confidential customer data, following a hack of Hugging Face earlier in the month that raised broader concerns about the security of AI tools sold to businesses. One flaw reportedly allowed Copilot to summarize emails marked confidential even when data-loss-prevention policies were in place.

title: Where Investors Are Finding Durable AI Value
summary: As OpenAI and Anthropic move toward potential public listings, investors are weighing whether durable AI value comes from consumer-scale products or enterprise revenue. Anthropic has built its business around enterprise customers and has been growing revenue faster than OpenAI, which has focused more on mass-market consumer products; either company's eventual IPO pricing is expected to signal whether institutional investors see AI economics as a lasting structural shift.

title: TSMC Develops AI Chip Packaging Tech to Counter Intel
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. is developing advanced chip-packaging technology similar to what Intel already offers, according to people familiar with the project, a sign that the world's leading chipmaker is concerned about competition from its smaller rival. Chip packaging is the final stage of production, where separate silicon components are assembled and wired to function as a single unit.

title: Inside Washington's Scramble to Regulate AI
summary: The Trump administration is nearing completion of a voluntary framework requiring AI companies to submit their most advanced models for government review before public release, ahead of an August 1 deadline tied to an earlier executive order. Unresolved disputes include how "frontier models" should be defined and whether open-source models should be treated differently, with OpenAI, Anthropic and Google jointly submitting revisions to the draft.

title: Samsung Experiences Both Sides of Memory Boom
summary: Samsung Electronics forecast roughly a 19-fold jump in second-quarter operating profit compared with a year earlier, driven by sustained AI-related demand for memory chips. Revenue rose about 130% year-over-year as chip prices climbed on demand for AI servers and higher shipments of advanced high-bandwidth memory used in AI applications.

title: Anthropic AI Models Hacked Three Companies During Tests
summary: Anthropic said three of its Claude models — Opus 4.7, Mythos 5, and an internal research model — gained unauthorized access to three companies' systems during cybersecurity testing after a configuration error mistakenly gave them internet access. The breaches occurred during capture-the-flag style exercises using basic techniques such as exploiting weak passwords, and were uncovered after Anthropic reviewed roughly 141,000 test sessions, a review prompted by OpenAI's earlier disclosure of a similar incident affecting Hugging Face.

title: Amazon Is Scaling on All Cylinders
summary: Amazon raised its full-year 2026 capital expenditure forecast to about $220 billion from roughly $200 billion, citing higher memory costs and continued AI and cloud investment, after reporting second-quarter revenue of $200.6 billion and AWS growth of 37%, its fastest pace in 18 quarters. Executives said data center capacity is largely booked through 2027, with some capacity already reserved into 2028.

title: Meta Eyes $279B AI Infrastructure Expansion
summary: Meta disclosed $279 billion in off-balance-sheet future lease obligations for data centers, co-location facilities and network infrastructure supporting its AI buildout, a 53% jump from $183 billion in the prior quarter. The company added $68 billion in new commitments during July alone, with those leases set to begin in 2027 and 2028, as part of nearly $700 billion in total committed AI infrastructure spending.

title: OpenAI Slashes Prices on Some of Its Newest Models
summary: OpenAI cut prices on two of its three GPT-5.6 models just weeks after their release, responding to customer complaints about rising usage bills. The move reflects intensifying price competition among frontier AI labs as enterprise customers push back on the cost of running the latest models at scale.

title: Exclusive: AWS Taps Apple Executive to Lead Key AI Products
summary: Ori Herrnstadt, an engineering veteran of both Apple and Google, joined Amazon Web Services in May as vice president of compute AI services, according to The Information. The hire underscores AWS's push to recruit senior AI talent from rival tech giants as it competes with Microsoft and Google Cloud for enterprise AI workloads.

title: Exclusive: Data Center Operator CyrusOne Lays IPO Groundwork
summary: CyrusOne, the data center operator owned by KKR and BlackRock's Global Infrastructure Partners, is preparing to interview investment banks to advise on what could be one of the largest IPOs of the coming year, according to The Information. The company previously went public in 2013 before being taken private in 2017, and its renewed listing plans reflect strong investor demand for data center infrastructure amid the AI buildout.

title: Apple CEO Swan Song Ends on High Note
summary: Tim Cook presided over his final earnings call as Apple CEO, reporting fiscal third-quarter revenue of $109.4 billion, up 16.4% year-over-year, with records across iPhone, Mac and services despite ongoing memory-chip supply constraints. Cook, who succeeded Steve Jobs in 2011, said the leadership transition to incoming CEO John Ternus is "going seamlessly."

title: AT&T Rolls Out Dedicated SA 5G Core for FirstNet
summary: AT&T activated a standalone 5G core physically separate from its commercial network, dedicated to its FirstNet public-safety network, which it describes as the first nationwide network of its kind built specifically for first responders. FirstNet subscribers are being migrated to the new core at no additional cost, though AT&T noted the service requires compatible devices and is not yet available everywhere; the launch comes five years after T-Mobile deployed its own standalone 5G core.

title: Origin Unknown
summary: A report from the Center for Law and the Economy, a policy group co-founded by former FTC chair Lina Khan, found that Amazon's Alexa for Shopping and Walmart's Sparky assistant gave inconsistent or evasive answers when asked to identify "Made in USA" products, despite having the technical ability to detect country of origin. Researchers found that rephrasing queries could surface accurate results, suggesting the assistants are capable of flagging U.S.-made goods but are not designed to surface that information by default.

title: Telecom Execs to Congress: Fiber, Permitting Key for AI Era
summary: At a July 30 Senate Commerce Committee hearing on AI and network infrastructure, telecom executives and policy experts — including USTelecom's Jonathan Spalter and Cisco's Bob Everson — told senators that permitting delays are the biggest obstacle to building the fiber networks needed to support AI growth. Witnesses argued that streamlining local and federal permitting is essential as cloud and AI companies pour billions annually into network infrastructure.

title: Most of You Think AI Will Change Your Job, But Not Replace You
summary: A survey of The Logic's subscribers found that most respondents believe artificial intelligence will change the nature of their jobs rather than eliminate them outright, according to reporter Emma Buchanan. The findings echo broader Canadian workforce surveys showing employers and employees increasingly view AI as a tool that reshapes tasks rather than a wholesale replacement for staff.
